newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kone warning, strong markka hit Finnish shares.
newsitem.headline: Kone warning, strong markka hit Finnish shares.

text.p: Shares extended Wednesday's losses on Thursday, hit by the strength in the markka amid talk of a link to ERM and a profit warning from Kone, brokers said.
Volume was solid, partly due to a massive deal in plastic pipe and furniture group Asko, as energy group Neste upped its stake to 26 percent from about 20 percent at the end of 1995.
Brokers expected the slide to continue on Friday, with the markka appearing to hold gains and Wall Street weak at the open.
Some brokers saw more downside in Kone -- even though the stock slumped more than 10 percent, or 55.00 markka, to end at 480.00 markka after it said 1996 profit woould be close to zero.
"Kone is still too expensive compared to projected earnings," one broker said.
But another said bargain-hunters could soon show up after Thursday's sharp fall.
Asko closed up 5.00 markka at 250 after hitting a two-year high 253.00 markka, but Neste lost 2.00 markka at 93.00 as some players had a negative view of the purchase, brokers said.
Nokia shed 0.50 markka at 193.00 in modest trade in line with its overnight losses on Wall Street.
Forestries were particularly hit by the markka's strength, brokers said.

"Some investors are probably selling Finnish forestries and buy Swedish," a broker said, adding that there were fears that Finnish forest sector's competitiveness could suffer if the markka was linked to Europe's exchange rate mechanism.
But another broker said UPM-Kymmene, which closed fair trade 0.80 markka at 98.70, was depressed by technical selling linked to derivatives trading.
Engineering group Santasalo lost some of Wednesday's strong gains in quiet trade, closing down 1.30 markka at 37.20 ahead of January-August results due on Friday at 0900/0600 GMT.
